avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction may reduce naltrexone levels; potential reduced efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use or monitor for decreased naltrexone effectiveness

avoid_supplements.name: Kava Kava
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Hepatotoxicity risk; may compound liver stress in patients with alcohol use disorder or cirrhosis

caution_supplements.name: Valerian Root
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential additive CNS depression; may increase sedation or dizziness
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for excessive CNS depression; advise patient of potential additive effects

caution_supplements.name: Milk Thistle
caution_supplements.mechanism: May support hepatic function but theoretical CYP3A4 modulation possible
caution_supplements.action: Generally safe; monitor liver function tests if used long-term

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol
avoid_foods.mechanism: Naltrexone blocks opioid receptors and may precipitate withdrawal; alcohol increases hepatotoxicity risk and CNS depression
avoid_foods.action: Absolute contraindication; counsel complete alcohol avoidance during treatment

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay naltrexone absorption and peak concentration timing
caution_foods.action: Take naltrexone consistently with or without food; maintain routine for consistent levels

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may increase naltrexone exposure slightly
caution_foods.action: Limit grapefruit juice consumption; not absolutely contraindicated but consistency advised

monitoring_notes: Monitor liver function tests regularly, especially in patients with hepatic impairment or history of liver disease. Counsel patients on strict alcohol avoidance and assess for opioid use to prevent precipitated withdrawal.
